comments.body:
Research: how major Python projects avoid by-path module identity collisions (2026-08-10)

The closest production-grade precedent is pytest itself. Its centralized import_path implementation does four things our 209 duplicated loaders do not: (1) derives a unique sys.modules name from the file path relative to a root in importlib mode; (2) returns an already-loaded module cache-first; (3) verifies that the cached module's __file__ matches the requested path and raises ImportPathMismatchError when it does not; and (4) inserts the module into sys.modules before exec_module. Source: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/main/src/_pytest/pathlib.py and https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/explanation/pythonpath.html#import-modes. The pytest docs explicitly say importlib mode generates a unique name from rootdir, while non-package test trees otherwise require globally unique module names.

CPython centralizes intentional fresh-import behavior in Lib/test/support/import_helper.py. import_fresh_module and CleanImport save affected sys.modules entries, remove them for the test, and restore them afterward. It does not let individual tests permanently overwrite shared aliases. Source: https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Lib/test/support/import_helper.py

These are highly active/popular precedents as of 2026-08-10: CPython ~74K stars and pytest ~14K, both updated today. The common architecture is an importable test-support module with explicit module-cache semantics, not hundreds of local loaders and not a fixture-only abstraction.

Recommended shape for rebar: tests/_support/import_path.py (inside an importable tests support package) callable at module scope and from fixtures. Give every source path a stable collision-free module name derived from its repository-relative path. If that name exists, return it only when resolved __file__ matches; otherwise fail loudly. Insert before exec and remove on failed execution. Provide a separate scoped fresh-import context that saves/restores sys.modules for the rare test that deliberately needs a second class identity. Do not silently overwrite a short shared name such as mutation or differ. This is broader and safer than merely adding cache-first checks to the existing aliases.

# 209 of 213 by-path test loaders are not cache-first, on keys shared by up to 9 files

## Provenance

Measured by AST walk over `tests/` while auditing bug 2bc7 (which repaired three files sharing the
`"mutation"` key). The audit's scope was that key; this is the surface it revealed.

```
total by-path loaders under tests/  : 213
using sys.modules.setdefault        :   0   (the original 9f0b/2bc7 defect is eradicated)
cache-first (name AND __file__)     :   4
```

The four are `test_differ.py`, `test_differ_conflict_resolution.py`,
`test_differ_quarantine_suppression.py` (2bc7's three) and `test_reconcile_filter.py::_stub_modules`.
2bc7 additionally fixed `test_differ_emits_probe.py` and `test_apply_list_of_mutations.py`.

## The collision surface

`sys.modules` keys registered by more than one test file:

```
outbound_differ   9 files        mutation    6 files
inbound_differ    8 files        reconcile   4 files
differ            5 files        applier     3 files
```

**None** of the loaders for `outbound_differ`, `inbound_differ`, `reconcile` or `applier` validates
`__file__`. The original bug surfaced on `mutation` only because that is where a cross-file
`isinstance` assertion happened to exist — the same latent coupling sits on keys with more registrants
and no such assertion to expose it.

## Why this is latent rather than broken

pytest executes module-by-module, so a file that overwrites a shared key is self-consistent while its
own tests run: its module-scoped fixture was built when its registration was current. The failure needs
two things to coincide — a cross-file identity comparison, and an execution order that puts the other
registrant first. 2bc7 was exactly that coincidence, and it presented as a macOS-only `isinstance`
failure on an object that WAS of the asserted class.

## What 2bc7 deliberately did not attempt

A shared helper, so the loader exists once. It is the right fix and it is not mechanical: the
registrants span `diffing/`, `mutate/`, `apply/`, `state/`, `fetch/`, `conflict/` and `orchestrate/`,
and pytest puts only each test's OWN directory on `sys.path`, so a bare-name import does not resolve
across them. Two workable shapes, both with costs:

* a module at the `tests/` root plus the `sys.path` plumbing `tests/_engine_path.py` already
  establishes — works for every caller including module-level constants;
* a conftest FIXTURE — inherited by subdirectories automatically, but cannot serve the call sites that
  load at module scope, and several do.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ONE cache-first by-path loader exists, reachable from every directory under `tests/` that needs
      it, with the `sys.path` mechanism it depends on documented at its definition
- [ ] every loader registering a key that MORE THAN ONE file registers is converted to it — the
      `outbound_differ`, `inbound_differ`, `differ`, `mutation`, `reconcile` and `applier` keys at
      minimum
- [ ] a guard test fails when a new by-path loader registers a SHARED key without validating
      `__file__`, so the count cannot regress silently (the audit above was a one-off scan; a scan
      nobody re-runs is not a guard)
- [ ] loaders that deliberately want an ISOLATED copy keep it, and say so — `test_mutation.py`
      returns an unregistered private copy and `test_differ.py` registers
      `mutation_for_diff_purity` under a distinct name; both are correct and must not be swept into
      the shared helper
- [ ] the full suite passes under a REVERSED collection order for the affected directories, not just
      the default alphabetical one

## Not urgent, and why

Nothing fails today. This is a latent-coupling cleanup whose value is that the next instance fails
locally and deterministically instead of as a platform-specific surprise in CI.
